item.description: On Saturday, Most Valuable Promotions celebrates its fifth anniversary. One of the feistiest upstarts in modern boxing has given a new platform to the world's best female fighters.

item.title: Why becoming heavyweight champ at 21 is a 'big deal' for Itauma
item.description: British heavyweight Moses Itauma fights Filip Hrgovic on Saturday for the vacant IBF world heavyweight title. If he wins the fight, Itauma will become the youngest heavyweight champion since Mike Tyson, and says the "expectations" are there for him to carry the flag for British boxing.

item.title: The big night for women's boxing
item.description: Female boxers Terri Harper, Mikaela Mayer, Chantelle Cameron and Caroline Dubois tell BBC Sport how Jake Paul's co-owned Most Valuable Promotions is "changing the sport forever" by providing "the fights the fans want to see."

item.title: From Love Island to Commonwealth gold for McConnell
item.description: Team Northern Ireland boxer Jon McConnell tells BBC Sport NI of his decision to reject Love Island to pursue his childhood dream of winning Commonwealth gold, which he achieved with a split decision win over Wales' Orlando Holley-Sotomi.
